issues.legal_issue: A written assignment of a decree transfers the decree rights according to the parties’ intention without requiring prior recognition by the executing court.
material_facts: The decree-holder executed a written deed assigning decree rights to the transferees.
The transferees applied to execute the decree, but the High Court held that the assignment had no effect until recognised by the court.
issues.conclusion: The assignment takes effect between the transferor and transferee when the deed intends the decree rights to pass; court recognition is not required to complete the assignment, though recognition is required for the transferee to proceed with execution.
issues.legal_principle: Order XXI Rule 16 of the Code of Civil Procedure enables a transferee to apply for execution and requires notice to the transferor and judgment-debtor, with execution stayed until their objections are heard; it does not make recognition a condition for the assignment to take effect. This is consistent with Dwar Buksh Sirkar v. Fatik Jali, Arvapalli Ramrao v. Kanumarlapudi Ranganayakulu, and Sadagopa Chariar v. Raghunatha Chariar, and contrary to Puthiandi Mammed v. Avalil Moidin, which the Court disapproved.

predicates.decree_execution_proceeding: The proceeding concerns execution of a decree by a person claiming as its transferee.
predicates.written_assignment_intended_to_transfer_: The decree-holder executed a written assignment intended to transfer rights under the decree.

issues.definition: When a decree is being executed and a written assignment is intended to transfer it, the assignment takes effect without prior court recognition.

issues.legal_issue: A judgment-debtor who has notice of an assignment cannot defeat the assignee’s execution rights by adjusting the decree with the original decree-holder.
material_facts: The transferees applied to execute the assigned decree, and notice of the application was issued to the judgment-debtor and the original decree-holder.
After that notice, the judgment-debtor and the original decree-holder agreed to a compromise, payment was made to the original decree-holder, and satisfaction was recorded.
The executing court had noted that the compromise would not affect any rights of the transferees under the assignment.
issues.conclusion: The post-notice adjustment did not bar execution by the transferees; an adjustment with the transferor cannot defeat the assignee’s rights once the judgment-debtor has notice of the transfer.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order XXI Rule 16 of the Code of Civil Procedure, a transferee may apply for execution after notice to the transferor and judgment-debtor. The transfer is effected by the assignment, and a judgment-debtor with notice cannot defeat the transferee’s rights by adjusting the decree with the transferor. A judgment-debtor who has no notice of the transfer and adjusts the decree before receiving notice under the rule is protected. The Court agreed with Dwar Buksh Sirkar v. Fatik Jali, Arvapalli Ramrao v. Kanumarlapudi Ranganayakulu, and Sadagopa Chariar v. Raghunatha Chariar.

predicates.decree_execution_proceeding_by_assignee: A person claiming as transferee seeks execution of a decree.
predicates.assigned_decree: The decree-holder transferred rights under the decree by assignment.
predicates.judgment_debtor_noticed_transfer_before_: The judgment-debtor knew of the transfer before adjusting the decree with the original decree-holder.

issues.definition: When an assignee seeks execution of a decree and the judgment-debtor knew of the assignment before adjusting the decree with the original decree-holder, that adjustment does not bar the assignee’s execution.
